title: API 570 Training in Mobile, AL: Piping Inspector Exam Prep
description: Self-paced API 570 exam prep for Mobile Bay piping inspectors: refinery and chlor-alkali lines, CUI in a wet climate, injection points and dead legs.
h1: API 570 Training in Mobile, Alabama: Piping Inspector Exam Prep for Refinery, Chemical Corridor and Marine Terminal Piping
html:
API 570 exam prep for piping inspectors around Mobile Bay

Piping is where most inspection hours on the Alabama and Mississippi coast actually go. A refinery's vessels can be counted in the hundreds, but its piping circuits run to many thousands of condition monitoring locations, and a chemical corridor with dozens of small production units multiplies that again. This page is for inspectors, NDT technicians, piping designers and operators in and around Mobile who are working toward API 570, the piping inspector certification, and who want to prepare without leaving the roster.

There is no Atlantis classroom in Mobile. The API 570 course is self-paced and online, with an instructor answering your questions as you work, so the material is the same whether you live in Saraland, Semmes or Ocean Springs. API sets the eligibility rules, administers the examination in person at Prometric test centres and issues the certification; the course prepares you for it and Atlantis does not hold API approval as a training provider.

Piping-heavy sites from Pascagoula to McIntosh

Across the state line, the Chevron refinery at Pascagoula is the largest piping system within reach of Mobile. EIA's survey for the start of 2026 lists it at 356,440 barrels per calendar day of crude distillation, with vacuum distillation of 334,000 barrels per stream day, delayed coking of 104,000, catalytic cracking of 88,700 fresh feed and gas oil hydrocracking of 121,000, plus low- and high-pressure reformers. Chevron's 2024 fact sheet counts 1,651 employees and 859 contractors, and the company says about 65 percent of the refinery's products leave by ship or barge from its marine terminal on Bayou Casotte. That is a lot of transfer and loading piping on top of the process units.

  • Vertex Refining Alabama, Saraland. The 88,000 barrel-per-day refinery north of Mobile has no coker or catalytic cracker but a gas oil hydrocracker, a high-pressure reformer and three desulfurization units in EIA's listing, and with them the reactor effluent, recycle gas and sour water piping that hydroprocessing brings.
  • Olin, McIntosh. A chlor-alkali plant producing chlorine, caustic soda, hydrochloric acid, hydrogen and bleach runs piping in some of the most material-sensitive services on the coast.
  • Evonik, Theodore. With 28 production plants on one site, Evonik's complex is a reminder that chemical piping is usually smaller in diameter, more varied in material and more often in stainless or alloy than refinery piping.

Chlor-alkali piping and the API 570 damage list

The Body of Knowledge for the February and June 2027 API 570 examinations limits RP 571 questions to 15 mechanisms. A McIntosh-style chlor-alkali plant touches more of them than most refinery units do:

  • Caustic corrosion and caustic stress corrosion cracking. Caustic lines at elevated temperature, steam-traced caustic lines and welds that were not stress relieved are the classic places to look.
  • Hydrochloric acid corrosion. Where hydrochloric acid is made, stored or recovered, water content decides how aggressive the service is, and dew-point conditions can turn a mild line severe.
  • Chloride stress corrosion cracking. Austenitic stainless piping in brine, or under wet insulation that leaches chlorides, cracks without much warning wall loss, so thickness data alone will not find it.
  • Galvanic corrosion. Plants that mix carbon steel, stainless, nickel alloys and titanium in one system create couples at flanges and transitions.

Refinery piping supplies the rest of the list: sulfidation in hot hydrocarbon lines, sour water corrosion in acidic sour water systems, amine stress corrosion cracking in amine units, erosion and erosion-corrosion at elbows and control valve outlets, and mechanical fatigue, including vibration-induced fatigue at small-bore branches near pumps and compressors. Underground and buried lines bring soil corrosion, and firewater and cooling water systems bring microbiologically influenced corrosion. The exam asks for the description, susceptible materials, critical factors, affected units and inspection methods of each, so learn them in that order.

Corrosion under insulation in a 67-inch rainfall climate

Mobile averaged 67.1 inches of precipitation a year over the 1991 to 2020 normals, on about 117 days with wet weather. Water gets under jacketing at every penetration, insulation support and damaged seam, and on the coast it comes with salt. RP 571 treats corrosion under insulation as a matter of operating temperature, cycling and water ingress rather than a single threshold, and the piping that worries Gulf inspectors most is the piping that runs in the range where water condenses and evaporates, or that cycles into it, for example during intermittent service or steam-out.

In an API 570 programme that becomes a ranking exercise. Lines in that susceptible range, with damaged jacketing, low points, vertical runs that collect water at the bottom, and insulation that cannot be removed without scaffolding, rise up the list. For stainless lines, look for chloride cracking as well as wall loss. The exam asks how CUI is found and which locations are likely; the practical skill on a Mobile unit is walking the line before deciding where to strip insulation, because the jacketing condition you see from the ground is the best single clue you have.

Injection points and dead legs on Gulf Coast units

API 570 treats injection points and dead legs as special cases because ordinary CML spacing misses them. At an injection point, water, caustic, corrosion inhibitor or neutralizer meets the process stream and the mixing zone can corrode far faster than the rest of the line. The code recommends treating the section around each injection point as its own inspection circuit, with upstream and downstream limits measured from the injection point and the flow direction changes after it, and its interval table gives injection points a separate, shorter maximum thickness interval than ordinary piping. Know where that paragraph and that table row sit in the open-book PDF.

Dead legs are the opposite problem: lines where flow has stopped, such as bypasses, closed drains, spare pump connections and piping left behind when a unit changed. Water and solids settle, the corrosion rate departs from the active line, and the dead section may sit at the bottom of a long run where nobody looks. A refinery that has changed the feed to a unit, as Saraland's hydrocracker did when it moved to renewable feed and back, is exactly where an inspector should ask which connections now see no flow.

Worked example: MAWP of a corroded line at the next inspection

The Body of Knowledge asks candidates to calculate the MAWP of corroded pipe while allowing for the corrosion expected before the next inspection. API 570 tells you to use the measured thickness minus twice the estimated corrosion loss up to that inspection.

  1. A 24 in. carbon steel line (OD 24.000 in.) has a lowest measured thickness of 0.330 in. at its worst CML. The governing corrosion rate is 0.008 in. per year and the next thickness inspection is planned in 5 years.
  2. Expected loss before that inspection: 0.008 × 5 = 0.040 in. Twice that is 0.080 in., so the thickness used is 0.330 − 0.080 = 0.250 in.
  3. The question gives S = 20,000 psi, E = 1.0, W = 1.0 and Y = 0.4. Rearranging the B31.3 pressure design equation t = PD ÷ 2(SEW + PY) for pressure gives P = 2SEWt ÷ (D − 2Yt).
  4. P = 2 × 20,000 × 1.0 × 1.0 × 0.250 ÷ (24.000 − 2 × 0.4 × 0.250) = 10,000 ÷ 23.800 = 420.2 psi.
  5. If the simpler Barlow form 2SEt ÷ D is specified instead, the answer is 10,000 ÷ 24 = 416.7 psi, slightly lower.

The most common wrong answer subtracts the loss once, giving t = 0.290 in. and a pressure near 488 psi, which overstates what the line can carry by the time the inspector returns. Always read whether the question wants the MAWP now, at the next inspection or at the end of the remaining life, and keep corrosion allowance and remaining life calculations separate.

Working a CML programme on a Mobile unit

Much of a piping inspector's week is spent on CML data rather than on the pipe itself. Each circuit groups piping of similar material, service and expected damage; each CML within it records thickness at a defined point; and the corrosion rate for each CML is calculated both long term, from the initial thickness, and short term, from the previous reading. API 570 leaves the inspector to judge which rate represents the current process, which is why changes of feed, new chemical treatment or a different crude slate matter so much. Remaining life is then calculated against the required thickness, the greater of the pressure design thickness and the owner's structural minimum, and the next interval is the shorter of half the remaining life and the class maximum.

The exam tests the rules; the job tests the judgement. Readings that jump between surveys usually mean a probe placed in a slightly different spot, a temperature correction missed or a pit found at last, and an inspector who can tell those apart saves a site from both unnecessary replacements and missed thinning.

Routes into API 570 from Mobile trades

API counts education plus experience gained in the last 10 years under an authorized inspection agency; the detail is on API 570 certification requirements. Engineering or technology graduates need one year of inspection, holders of a two-year engineering or technology degree or certificate two years including one in inspection, high school graduates three, and those with no formal education five or more.

  • Pipe welders. Bishop State Community College offers a pipe welding technology short-term certificate alongside its welding associate degree. A short welding certificate is unlikely to count as a two-year technology credential, so plan on the high school route unless API confirms otherwise, and record the repair and fabrication piping work you did.
  • NDT technicians. UT thickness readings on CMLs are close to the work API 570 describes, but the experience API wants is inspection: assessing the results against the code and recommending what happens next.
  • Operators and piping designers. Operations and design experience on piping can count toward the longer routes, provided at least one year of it is supervision or performance of inspection.

Studying the open-book half on a rotating schedule

About a third of the API 570 examination is open book, and most of the lost marks there are lost to searching. B31.3 is the long document: learn the tables for allowable stress and joint quality factors, the pressure design paragraphs, the leak test paragraphs, the impact test rules and the preheat and heat treatment tables. B16.5 needs its material group table and the pressure-temperature ratings for each group, because flange rating questions are a reliable source of marks. Branch reinforcement and its sample calculations are excluded from the current Body of Knowledge, so do not spend study hours there.

A practical plan for a rotating shift is to use day shifts for reading, night shifts or quiet periods for short question sets, and days off for full timed papers, sending the instructor any question that takes more than a few minutes to resolve. Atlantis also offers AWS CWI exam preparation at AWS CWI exam prep in Mobile for welding inspectors whose work leans toward fabrication.

Sponsoring a piping inspection group in Mobile

Employers can enrol several candidates together, and fees are quoted on request. For a site with a large CML backlog the business case is straightforward: certified API 570 inspectors can take on the inspector's role the code describes, from evaluating thickness data to authorizing repair work under the owner's programme. Each candidate applies to API individually, so give each one a supervisor who can document piping inspection duties accurately, and stagger applications across exam windows so that not every senior technician is studying in the same months.

faq.q: Is there an API 570 course I can attend in a classroom in Mobile?
faq.a: No. There is no Atlantis classroom in Mobile, and the API 570 course runs self-paced online, with instructor Q&A whenever a code paragraph or calculation does not make sense. You study from home or the plant at your own pace and then sit the examination in person at a Prometric test centre once API has accepted your application. API grades the exam and issues the certification.

faq.q: Does piping at a chlor-alkali plant such as McIntosh fall under API 570?
faq.a: API 570 applies to in-service piping in the refining and chemical process industries, so a chlor-alkali plant can adopt it for its process piping. Its corrosion-rate and thickness rules are written around metal loss, so lined and non-metallic lines need the owner's procedures to say how they are assessed. The exam's damage list includes caustic corrosion, caustic cracking, hydrochloric acid corrosion and chloride cracking, which cover a large part of chlor-alkali piping.

faq.q: How much does Mobile's rainfall change the way CUI is inspected?
faq.a: It raises the priority of insulated lines operating in, or cycling through, the range where moisture condenses and evaporates, and it shortens the life of jacketing and sealing. Mobile averages about 67 inches of precipitation a year. Inspection planning starts with susceptible temperature, damaged jacketing, low points and penetrations, then uses stripping, profile radiography or other methods your owner approves to confirm what is underneath.

faq.q: Why does API 570 treat injection points differently from the rest of a line?
faq.a: Because the mixing zone around an injection point can corrode much faster than the line upstream or far downstream. API 570 recommends inspecting that section as its own circuit with defined upstream and downstream limits and gives injection points their own maximum thickness interval in the interval table. On the exam, find that paragraph and that row quickly in the open-book PDF.

faq.q: What does twice the corrosion loss mean in an API 570 MAWP question?
faq.a: When you calculate the MAWP a corroded line can carry until the next inspection, API 570 has you subtract twice the corrosion expected before that inspection from the measured thickness. With a rate of 0.008 in. per year and five years to the next inspection, you subtract 0.080 in., not 0.040 in. Then apply the pressure equation the question specifies.

faq.q: Can a pipe welder trained at Bishop State qualify for API 570?
faq.a: Yes, with enough experience. A short welding certificate is unlikely to be accepted as a two-year engineering or technology credential, so most welders apply on the high school route, which needs three years of piping experience including one year supervising or performing inspection. Fabrication and repair experience counts toward the total; the year of inspection must be documented by the employer.

faq.q: Should a Mobile inspector take API 570 or API 510 first?
faq.a: Take the one that matches the work you do now, because your experience must be documented against that code. On the corridor many contract inspectors start with API 570, since piping CML programmes employ more people than vessel inspection, and add API 510 later. The second exam is easier because API 571, RP 577, Section V and Section IX overlap between the two.

faq.q: Where is the nearest place to sit the API 570 exam from Mobile?
faq.a: Prometric lists test centres in and around Mobile, and you choose one when you book your seat after API approves your application. Bring the identification Prometric asks for; you cannot bring papers, notes or code books. The open-book documents are on the computer as PDFs, which is why practising searches in electronic files matters.
